reader.requirement: At --std 85, a sequential file whose FD has no CODE-SET clause holds its data on the medium in the native character set: every record character is written in its native encoding and read back as the same native character, with no conversion.
reader.edition-search: grep DialectLevel|Dialect in SequentialConnector.cs, CodeSetConversion.cs and FileCharacterSet.cs found none; EmitCodeSetRegistration emits nothing when CodeSetCorrespondence is null (no clause, or a NATIVE alphabet), so the connector's conversion stays null at every edition
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_bf03_05 covers the native twin reading EBCDIC codes and an AB012 round trip; not the full native byte range, the HIGH-VALUE character, or CODE-SET IS a NATIVE alphabet

probes.printed: WRITE 00; every native ordinal 1..255 round trips; DIFFERS AT ORDINAL 256; HIGH-VALUE KEPT; CHAR(256) IS NOT HIGH-VALUE; BAD 001
probes.expected: native characters written and read back unchanged

probes.printed: no CODE-SET: medium E9 F0, PLAIN ROUND TRIP; CODE-SET IS a NATIVE alphabet: medium E9 F0, NAT ROUND TRIP
probes.expected: the native set on the medium, the same as a NATIVE alphabet

probes.printed: the file without CODE-SET (FR, FVR) sees the EBCDIC codes another FD wrote (129 92 130 ...; 231), unconverted
probes.expected: no conversion when the clause is absent

citations.check: OK  §1985:VII.3.4.4 GR2  (3.4.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR2

reader.notes: The connector carries no conversion when the clause is absent, and the medium holds the native DISPLAY encoding. Doubt stated: native U+00FF (CHAR(256)) shares the byte 0xFF with HIGH-VALUE and reads back as HIGH-VALUE (cs03); that is the owner-accepted cost of the native DISPLAY encoding (kb/Work R52, docs/conformance/7/DOC-A.1-31.md), a property of the implementor-defined native encoding rather than of this rule, so it is not counted as a divergence here.

refuter.evidence: csnat.cob at --std 85: OBJECT-COMPUTER PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE IS an EBCDIC alphabet, a file without CODE-SET written '1a$' 'Ab~' and SORT USING it GIVING another file without CODE-SET: both media hold native bytes (31 61 24 41 62 7e; sorted 41 62 7e 31 61 24, EBCDIC order letters before digits), so neither the collating alphabet nor SORT leaks a conversion onto a file without the clause; cssame.cob and cssort.cob read raw native codes through FDs without CODE-SET.
